question.text: Let $f: X \rightarrow Y$ and $A, B$ are non-void subsets of $Y$, then (where the symbols have their usual interpretation)

options.text: $f^{-1}(A)-f^{-1}(B) \supset f^{-1}(A-B)$ but the opposite does not hold.
$f^{-1}(A)-f^{-1}(B) \subset f^{-1}(A-B)$ but the opposite does not hold.

solution.text: Let A={1,2,3} and B={2,3,4} here, $f^{-1}(3)=1$ $f^{-1}(4)=2$ and $f^{-1}(2)=3$ It is clear that option (C) $f^{-1}(A-B)=f^{-1}(A)$ $-f^{-1}(B)$ is correct.
